transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I just haven’t been feeling like myself. It’s not anything dramatic, I don’t think, but I used to really enjoy things—painting, hiking, singing in choir, Sunday get-togethers with my family—and lately even if I have a free hour, I just sort of sit there and can’t make myself care about any of it. I thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Have you been experiencing a lack of pleasure in activities that you normally enjoy?

Yes… I think that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I used to make time for things I really loved—painting, hiking, choir, even Sunday family get-togethers—and now, if I have a free hour, I mostly just sit there. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it. It just doesn’t feel like me.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time?

Yes… I mean, I try not to show it, especially at school, but most days it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in a classroom full of students, or even at home with my husband, and I still feel sort of hollow… like I’m close to tears for no clear reason. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
Um… I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed anything major, at least not that I could say for sure. My clothes seem mostly the same, I think. Should I have been keeping track?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes… a bit. Well, more than a bit, I guess. My sleep’s been really inconsistent for months. I’ll lie there replaying details about grants and things I need to get right, and then I wake up around three or four and can’t always get back to sleep. Even on nights when I technically sleep longer, I still get up feeling like I didn’t really rest. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess… it’s been building for about eight months now. It seemed to start around when I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative. I kept thinking it was just stress and that I’d adjust, but… it hasn’t really lifted. Is that helpful?
Have you been experiencing any thoughts of death or suicide?

I… I wouldn’t say I want to hurt myself, exactly. I haven’t made any kind of plan. But… on some of the really late nights in the studio, I do catch myself thinking it might be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. That sounds awful to say out loud.

It scared me enough that I told my husband I couldn’t keep handling those thoughts by myself. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant loss of energy or fatigue?

I’m not sure… I mean, I do get tired, but I’ve been telling myself that’s just from being busy and not sleeping great. I wouldn’t want to overstate it.

I can still get through what I need to do most days, so… I don’t know if it counts as a significant loss of energy. Maybe some fatigue, but I’m not sure how much is unusual. Does that answer it okay?
Would you say your feelings of sadness or being down are mild, or are they interfering more significantly with your daily life?

I want to say mild, because I can still show up and do what I’m supposed to do… but honestly, it feels more than that most days.

It’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in a classroom full of students, or at home with my husband, and still feel sort of hollow… like I’m right on the edge of crying. So yes, I think it is interfering more than I want to admit. Does that make sense?
Would you say that most days, you're able to find some moments of happiness or feeling okay, even if they're brief?

I try to look for those moments, I really do. And I guess there are brief times where I feel… okay-ish. But what finally made me come in is that I don’t feel like myself anymore.

I used to make time for painting, hiking, choir, Sunday family things… and now even if I have a free hour, I just sort of sit there. I can’t seem to care about any of it the way I used to. I don’t know if that’s what you’re asking, but it feels like I’ve lost access to the parts of me that used to feel happy.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are present most of the day?

Yes… I think so. I keep wanting to say it comes and goes, because that sounds less dramatic, but most days it really is there for a lot of the day.

It’s like that heavy gray film I mentioned — even when I’m in the classroom with students, or at home with my husband, I can still feel hollow and kind of close to tears. I’m sorry if I’m not explaining it well, but yes, I’d say it’s present most of the day.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are severe enough to markedly interfere with your daily life?

I guess… yes, more than I’d like to admit.

I’m still trying to keep things going, but I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding some of the student workshops because I just can’t keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. I feel embarrassed saying that.

And at home, my husband has had to step in more. I withdraw from family plans, and sometimes I don’t feel like I can safely just push through on my own. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… yes, it is interfering pretty significantly.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about yourself or your situation?

A little, yes… I mean, maybe more than a little. I don’t want to sound self-pitying.

When anything goes wrong with the curriculum project, even something small, I immediately start thinking I’m letting the students down. Like I should be doing better for them. And then it turns into this bigger thing, like… my parents sacrificed a lot for me to have opportunities like this, and I’m wasting it somehow.

I know that may not be completely fair or logical, but it feels very real in the moment. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself moving or talking much slower, and I don’t think I’m pacing or anything like that.

Maybe I’m a bit quieter sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing. If anything, other people haven’t really pointed it out to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are severely debilitating, interfering with nearly all aspects of your daily life?

I don’t know if I’d say “nearly all aspects,” because I’m still trying to function… but it’s definitely affecting a lot.

I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding some of the student workshops because I just don’t feel like I can keep up with those responsibilities the way I used to. And at home, my husband has had to take on more because I tend to pull back from family plans.

I guess the part I feel a little ashamed saying is that sometimes I don’t feel safe just forcing myself through it alone. So… maybe not completely debilitating in every area, but it is interfering pretty seriously.

Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are making it difficult for you to perform even the smallest tasks, like taking care of your personal hygiene or getting dressed in the morning?

Not usually with the very smallest things, no… I mean, I’m still getting dressed and managing basic hygiene most days.

It’s more that the bigger responsibilities have started slipping. I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding student workshops because I just don’t feel like I can keep up the way I used to. And at home, my husband has had to step in more because I pull back from family plans.

I feel a bit embarrassed saying that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I also don’t think I’m handling it as well as I should. Sometimes I don’t feel safe just pushing through it alone, if that makes sense.
Would you say that there are any times during the day when you feel completely free of sadness or emptiness?

Not completely, no… I wish I could say there are clear times when it lifts, but most days it’s more like there’s this heavy gray film over everything.

Even when I’m in a classroom with students, or at home with my husband, I can still feel kind of hollow… and closer to tears than I probably look. I can distract myself for a little while, maybe, but I don’t know that I feel truly free of it. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are making everyday activities, like cooking or cleaning, feel like too much to handle?

Some everyday things do feel harder, yes… I’m still doing some of them, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it takes a lot more out of me than it should.

The bigger problem is that I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding some student workshops because I just don’t feel like I can keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. At home, my husband has had to step in more because I pull back from family plans.

I feel a little embarrassed saying that… like maybe I should be managing better. But sometimes I don’t feel safe just trying to push through it alone. Does that make sense?
Would you describe your current feelings of sadness or emptiness as overwhelming, to the point where you feel like you're barely able to cope?

I… I think “overwhelming” might be fair, yes, though I don’t want to sound dramatic.

Most days it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing in a classroom full of students, or just at home with my husband, and still feel hollow… and close to tears. I’m coping in the sense that I’m still getting through parts of the day, but it feels like I’m only just managing sometimes.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are consistently severe enough to cause significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning?

Yes… I think it has been significant, even if I keep wanting to say I’m “managing.”

I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding student workshops because I just don’t feel like I can keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. And at home, my husband has had to take on more because I withdraw from family plans.

I feel a bit ashamed saying that, honestly. I don’t want it to sound like I’m not trying. But sometimes I don’t feel safe just pushing through it alone, if that answers what you’re asking.

I’m coping in the sense that I’m still getting through parts of the day, but it feels like I’m only just managing sometimes.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive episode
doctor.question: Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are consistently severe enough to cause significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've missed several teaching sessions and have been avoiding student workshops because I can't keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. At home, my husband has had to step in more because I withdraw from family plans and don't feel safe pushing through alone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are causing significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning, which directly matches Functional Impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it has been significant, even if I keep wanting to say I’m “managing.”

I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding student workshops because I just don’t feel like I can keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. And at home, my husband has had to take on more because I withdraw from family plans.

I feel a bit ashamed saying that, honestly. I don’t want it to sound like I’m not trying. But sometimes I don’t feel safe just pushing through it alone, if that answers what you’re asking.
